clue.text: Singer's money runs out

indicators.note: out here means the runs go out of the money, leaving it without that letter

parts.note: brass is informal British slang for money
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A singer has spent all their cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Singer stands for 'is', a link. 'out' removes R (runs) from BRASS.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass is a male vocalist with the lowest voice range, so a kind of singer.

clue.text: A sub, reportedly unescorted

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said or heard, so the words a loan are spoken

parts.note: a sub is a small advance of money, a loan, so 'a sub' is 'a loan'

explanation.surface: A submarine, so they say, travels without escort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sub' suggests a submarine, but it is the British informal word for an advance on wages.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unescorted has no companion with them, which is being on one's own.

clue.text: People not social distancing in game?

definitions.meaning: cryptically, people who invade one another's space, ignoring the rule to keep apart

explanation.surface: Is there a game about people who ignore social distancing?
explanation.definitionFit: Those who intrude on personal space are whimsically space invaders, also the name of a famous video game.

clue.text: Manage ably for so long

parts.note: to fare is to get on or manage
ably means well

explanation.surface: Coping competently for such a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so long' looks like a time span, but it is the goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: So long is an informal parting phrase, a goodbye just like farewell.

clue.text: Natural ability shown by learner in market

indicators.note: in places the learner letter within the word for market

parts.note: a fair is a market or trading gathering
L is the learner driver's plate letter

explanation.surface: A trainee shows natural talent while working in a market.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair is an instinctive talent or aptitude for something.

clue.text: Issue on subject of tenancy

parts.note: re means concerning, on the subject of
a lease is a tenancy agreement

explanation.surface: A problem raised about a tenancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' reads as a noun, a problem, but it is the verb, to put out.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue a record or statement is to release it to the public.

clue.text: Women's rowing crew taking up sport

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen
taking up means lifting

explanation.surface: A women's rowing crew adopts a new sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking up' seems to mean starting a hobby, but it gives LIFTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Weightlifting is an Olympic strength sport of raising barbells.

clue.text: Saying few words, the French Commander-in-Chief holding on

parts.note: la is a French word for the

indicators.note: holding means the commander's letters hold the word on inside them

explanation.surface: A French commander-in-chief who barely speaks while he holds on.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic describes terse speech, using very few words, after the clipped Spartans of Laconia.

clue.text: Reorganisation of NATO unlikely, so don't mention it

indicators.note: a reorganisation rearranges the parts, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: a tall story is an unlikely one, so tall means unlikely

explanation.surface: A NATO restructure is improbable, so keep quiet about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reorganisation of' turns NATO into NOTA. 'so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are polite replies to thanks, waving away any gratitude.

clue.text: Measure some chinchillas

indicators.note: some means only part of the word chinchillas is taken

explanation.surface: Measuring a few chinchillas.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is an imperial unit of length, a measure.

clue.text: Incredibly remote shooting star

indicators.note: incredibly suggests something wildly unbelievable, so the letters of remote are scrambled

explanation.surface: A shooting star seen very far away.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor is the streak of light from space debris burning up, popularly a shooting star.

clue.text: Spoil mother rotten, initially

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of rotten is used

explanation.surface: Spoiling one's mother rotten from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoil ... rotten' reads as a single idiom for pampering, but only Spoil is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to damage or spoil it.

clue.text: Within easy reach of a labourer saving time

indicators.note: saving here means keeping, holding the time letter within

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker or labourer

explanation.surface: Something close by for a worker who wants to save time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' puts T inside A HAND. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at hand is nearby and readily available.

clue.text: Game dart players may play constantly?

definitions.meaning: a darts game hitting each number from 1 to 20 in turn

explanation.surface: Darts players could play this game nonstop.
explanation.definitionFit: Working around the clock means without a break, all day and night, the dartboard game shares the name.

clue.text: Personal objective in move that backfired?

parts.note: own means personal, belonging to oneself
a goal is an objective or aim

explanation.surface: A personal aim pursued through a plan that went wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: An own goal, in football scoring for the opposition, figuratively an action that harms its maker.

clue.text: Some attending banquet old official scolded

indicators.note: some of those attending means only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Some guests at the banquet were reprimanded by an elderly official.
explanation.definitionFit: Told off is an idiom for reprimanded or rebuked.

clue.text: Tackle satirical sketch taking off Society

indicators.note: taking off means removing, so the society letter is dropped from the sketch

parts.note: a skit is a short satirical sketch

explanation.surface: Tackling a satirical sketch that sends up high society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackle' reads as a verb but is the noun, gear; 'taking off' also suggests mimicry.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle and kit both mean equipment, as in fishing tackle.

clue.text: Call for English translation of Latin

indicators.note: a translation turns words into a new form, so the letters of Latin are rearranged

explanation.surface: A request for an English rendering of a Latin text.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail something is to require or necessitate it.

clue.text: Really popular female performance

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: A truly well-liked show by a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: In fact is used to stress the truth of a statement, like actually.

clue.text: Model and I hand out cards

parts.note: to deal is to distribute playing cards

explanation.surface: A fashion model and I share out a deck of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a perfect example to follow, a model or paragon.

clue.text: Fine the Parisian parked in vehicle

indicators.note: parked in means set inside, so the French article sits within the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
le is French for the, the word a Parisian would use

explanation.surface: A Parisian is fined for parking in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like a parking penalty, but means clear, as in fine weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine weather is clear weather, without cloud or rain.

clue.text: Bond actor picked up extra

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the actor's name is spoken

parts.note: Roger Moore played James Bond in seven films

explanation.surface: An actor who played James Bond was hired as an extra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extra' suggests a film walk-on, but it means additional.
explanation.definitionFit: More means additional or further, an extra amount.

clue.text: Pithy joke about European passenger ship

parts.note: on means about or concerning
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A short gag about a European cruise ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-liner is a brief witty remark delivered in a single sentence.

clue.text: Completely happy English composer? Almost completely

parts.note: Sir Arthur Bliss was an English composer, Master of the Queen's Music

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: full means complete or completely

explanation.surface: Is an English composer happy? Almost entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: Blissful means filled with perfect joy, utterly happy.

clue.text: Hollywood star disposing of old clothes

indicators.note: disposing of means getting rid of, so the old letter goes

parts.note: Greta Garbo was a Hollywood film star

explanation.surface: A Hollywood star throws away old clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old clothes' reads as one phrase, but old is the O removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing, especially a distinctive outfit.
